structs.size_evidence: NOT directly proven. Their spacing is 464, which equals game-test FlightDynamicsRotorSystem size (0x1D0). game-test rotor blades sit at rotor offset 0xC8 = 200, so MainRotor base = 1464-200 = 1264 and TailRotor base = 1728. HelicopterDynamics' first own member is m_MainRotor (game-test 0x520 = FlightDynamics end), so FlightDynamics own size = 1264. Candidate 1264; game-test 1312 minus 48 (the m_GforceMagnitude 4 bytes + 4 pad are not in Replay FlightDynamics). Replay-side check still open: HelicopterDynamics owner should confirm m_MainRotor at 1264.

structs.notes: Replay FlightDynamics = game-test FlightDynamics shifted by -40 for members 688..1252 (confirmed on Position, Velocity, status, quaternions, sound hashes, FlyByWire enable, Raw and FBW control arrays). The IDA layout (22272 bytes) is wrong: its m_unk members at 16..652 belong to the BgVehiclePhysics base, and m_unk1308 and later are not FlightDynamics members. The Replay base is 688 bytes (FlightDynamics own fields begin at 688); this conflicts with A080's BgVehiclePhysics estimate of 1960, so the BgVehiclePhysics owner needs to check. The FixUpLoad access at 2780 (a1 + _pad92C[432], SoundData::Setup@0x140D1C380) is not a FlightDynamics member: FlightDynamics ends at about 1264. It is most likely a HelicopterDynamics or whole-vehicle object reached through the FD vtable. Replay max access for FlightDynamics-typed code is 1252 (sound and gyro vectors). Coordinator: do not set the size from replay_max_access_end (2780).
